sources: Artificial Analysis API (Intelligence Index, blended price, speed)

counterevidence: List prices, not the committed-use prices large buyers pay; the Intelligence Index is re-based between Artificial Analysis versions; the top decile moves as models are added and dropped; unpriced models are excluded.
definition: On each price change date, the lowest Artificial Analysis blended list price (USD per million tokens, 3:1 input to output) divided by the model's Intelligence Index, among models in the top decile of the index. Derived metric aa_frontier_price_per_point.

direction_rule.rationale: Four price change-points; a move under $0.0006 per million tokens per index point (about a tenth of the 11 Sep 2026 level) is one model's repricing. Rising = labs keeping the surplus from capability gains.

name: Price per unit of capability (cheapest near-frontier model, Artificial Analysis)
stale_reason: Change-point series: a quiet month means prices held; fetch freshness is on /sources.

status_events.author: claude
status_events.reason: First price snapshot, 11 Sep 2026: the cheapest model in the top decile of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, GLM-5.3 Flash (index 41.9, $0.237 per million blended tokens), costs about $0.0057 per million tokens per index point. The series records price change-points, so a direction needs four more of them; not yet measurable until then.

timing_rationale: Coincident: a model's price and index arrive together at release, so the ratio moves when the market does.
tracker_interpretation: The series records price change-points from 11 September 2026; a direction needs several of them. The cheapest near-frontier model is often an open-weight one, so this reads the whole model layer, not only the frontier labs.
why_it_matters: The same capture proxy as the METR-hour price on an independent capability axis that covers hundreds of models, refreshed daily. Falling means the surplus from better models is passed on; flat or rising means labs keep it.
